_comment: Design-phase fixture for the Sky screen bake-off. Hand-written, plausible Columbia CS data. Deliberately exercises every visual state: completed, eligible_now, eligible_next (1 semester out), eligible_later (2+ out), note-leaf prereq advisories, absent CULPA data, and courses shared across pathways.

COMS W1004.title: Introduction to Computer Science and Programming in Java

culpa.review_excerpt: Perfect on-ramp; the weekly labs carry the course.

COMS W1004.description_excerpt: Fundamentals of computer science: algorithmic problem solving, data abstraction, and program design in Java.

COMS W3134.title: Data Structures in Java

culpa.review_excerpt: The gateway course; every later class assumes you aced this.

COMS W3134.description_excerpt: Data types and structures: arrays, stacks, linked lists, trees, graphs, and their use in fundamental algorithms.

COMS W3203.title: Discrete Mathematics
COMS W3203.description_excerpt: Logic, sets, functions, relations, induction, counting, and graph theory as the mathematical basis of computer science.

MATH UN1101.title: Calculus I
MATH UN1101.description_excerpt: Limits, derivatives, and integrals of functions of one variable.

MATH UN1102.title: Calculus II
MATH UN1102.description_excerpt: Techniques of integration, sequences and series, and applications.

COMS W3157.title: Advanced Programming

culpa.review_excerpt: Brutal workload, but you come out actually knowing C and the shell.

COMS W3157.description_excerpt: C programming, UNIX tools, systems-level development practice, and a team project.

COMS W3261.title: Computer Science Theory

culpa.review_excerpt: Dry but essential; automata finally click in week six.

COMS W3261.description_excerpt: Regular and context-free languages, Turing machines, computability, and complexity.

CSEE W3827.title: Fundamentals of Computer Systems
CSEE W3827.description_excerpt: Boolean logic, processor design, memory hierarchy, and assembly-level programming.

COMS W4111.title: Introduction to Databases

culpa.review_excerpt: The project is the whole course; start the schema early.

COMS W4111.description_excerpt: The relational model, SQL, database design, and transaction fundamentals.

COMS W3251.title: Computational Linear Algebra
COMS W3251.description_excerpt: Linear algebra from a computational perspective: matrices, decompositions, and numerical methods.

COMS W4170.title: User Interface Design

culpa.review_excerpt: Portfolio-ready projects and genuinely useful critique sessions.

COMS W4170.description_excerpt: Human-centered design process, prototyping, and evaluation of interactive systems.

COMS W4995.title: Topics: Human-Centered Machine Learning
COMS W4995.prereq_note: Instructor permission required for students without ML background.
COMS W4995.description_excerpt: Seminar on the design and evaluation of machine learning systems that people use directly.

COMS W4118.title: Operating Systems

culpa.review_excerpt: The kernel assignments are the hardest and best thing in the major.

COMS W4118.description_excerpt: Processes, scheduling, memory management, file systems, and kernel programming.

COMS W4701.title: Artificial Intelligence

culpa.review_excerpt: Search and games are fun; the pace picks up sharply after the midterm.

COMS W4701.description_excerpt: Search, knowledge representation, probabilistic reasoning, and introductory machine learning.

COMS W4115.title: Programming Languages and Translators
COMS W4115.description_excerpt: Language design and implementation: lexing, parsing, semantic analysis, and code generation, with a team compiler project.

COMS W4156.title: Advanced Software Engineering
COMS W4156.description_excerpt: Software lifecycle at scale: design, testing, CI, and a semester-long team service project.

COMS W4119.title: Computer Networks
COMS W4119.description_excerpt: Protocol layering, routing, congestion control, and socket programming.

COMS W4172.title: 3D User Interfaces and Augmented Reality
COMS W4172.description_excerpt: Interaction techniques and system design for 3D, VR, and AR interfaces.

COMS W4771.title: Machine Learning
COMS W4771.prereq_note: Probability and statistics prerequisite may be satisfied by instructor permission.

culpa.review_excerpt: Mathematically demanding and worth every problem set.

COMS W4771.description_excerpt: Supervised and unsupervised learning, kernels, model selection, and generalization theory.

COMS W4113.title: Fundamentals of Large-Scale Distributed Systems
COMS W4113.description_excerpt: Consistency, replication, fault tolerance, and consensus in distributed systems.

COMS W4705.title: Natural Language Processing

culpa.review_excerpt: Great arc from n-grams to transformers in one semester.

COMS W4705.description_excerpt: Language modeling, parsing, and modern neural approaches to text understanding.

COMS W4731.title: Computer Vision
COMS W4731.description_excerpt: Image formation, feature detection, recognition, and deep learning for vision.

pathways.name: Intelligent Systems
pathways.thesis: Build toward research-grade AI by pairing the theory core with the full ML course sequence. Every semester unlocks the next rung of the AI ladder.

nodes.fit_reasoning: Automata and complexity underpin the formal side of AI you said you wanted; taking it now unlocks W4701 next semester.
Linear algebra is the single biggest predictor of ML success; the computational framing fits your hands-on preference.
The AI survey ties your interest in agents directly to search and probabilistic reasoning.
Systems literacy keeps the ML path grounded and satisfies the systems core early.
The rigorous ML core; your linear algebra from semester one makes the math load manageable.
Real ML work lives on real data; databases round out the applied skill set.
NLP matches your stated interest in language interfaces and builds directly on W4701.
Vision completes an ML portfolio that covers the two dominant application domains.

pathways.name: Systems Builder
pathways.thesis: Go deep on how computers actually work, from C and hardware up through kernels, networks, and distributed systems. The classic infrastructure engineer arc.

nodes.fit_reasoning: The C and UNIX foundation every later systems course assumes; its workload is heaviest, so it goes first.
Hardware fundamentals taken alongside W3157 give you the full stack picture in one semester.
The kernel course is the heart of this pathway; both prerequisites land the semester before.
Theory core requirement placed where it balances the OS workload.
Distributed systems is where your interest in large-scale infrastructure pays off; OS is the direct prerequisite.
Networks alongside distributed systems is the classic pairing; the two courses reinforce each other weekly.
Team engineering practice converts your systems depth into shippable software.
The compiler project is the capstone-grade build this pathway has been preparing you for.

pathways.name: Human-Centered Computing
pathways.thesis: Pair the CS core with design, HCI, and applied ML so you graduate building products people actually want to use.

nodes.fit_reasoning: UI design directly serves your product-design career direction and opens the HCI sequence.
Engineering credibility for a design-leaning path; keeps every systems door open.
Every product you described is data-backed; databases are the enabling skill.
Human-centered ML sits exactly at the intersection you described; note the instructor-permission requirement.
AR interfaces extend W4170 into the emerging interaction platforms you mentioned.
Theory core requirement, placed late where the workload is lighter.
Team software engineering mirrors how product teams actually ship.
An AI foundation keeps the ML-adjacent product roles within reach.
